Primary Request and Intent: **Request 1 — Samson Moges Website (Complete Redesign):** Build a very modern, elegant, professional academic portfolio for Samson Tilahun Moges (postdoctoral space physicist). Reference style: academicpages.github.io. Push to GitHub. Scholar profile: https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=Weg1NwQAAAAJ&hl=en **Request 2 — Aleka Ayalew Website (New Build):** Create the exact same website design but with different information for Aleka Melese Ayalew. Repo: `/scratch/gdemil24/aleka-ayalew.github.io/`. Scholar: https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=Yda5OkEAAAAJ&hl=en, University: https://www.oulu.fi/en/researchers/aleka-melese-ayalew, LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/aleka-melese/ **Request 3 — Fix Citation Count:** User confirmed Aleka's Google Scholar shows 528 citations (not 292 as initially populated). **Request 4 — Live Citation Counter:** Avoid hardcoding citations; use a live counter from Google Scholar if possible, so it updates automatically when new citations come in. **Request 5 — Profile Photo:** Use Aleka's real profile photo (provided as image, saved at `/scratch/gdemil24/aleka-ayalew.github.io/aleka.jpg`) instead of the "AM" monogram placeholder. **Request 6 — Fix URL Hash:** URL shows `https://aleka-ayalew.github.io/#hero` instead of clean `https://aleka-ayalew.github.io/` on homepage. Fix for both sites. --- 2. Key Technical Concepts: - Pure static HTML/CSS/JS site (no build tools, GitHub Pages compatible) - "Arctic Aurora" design system: deep navy (`#050c1a`) + teal (`#00c8b4`) + gold (`#f0a500`) - CSS Custom Properties with `[data-theme="dark"]` / `[data-theme="light"]` dual-theme architecture - CSS-only aurora animation (layered radial-gradient divs with `@keyframes`) - Dark/light mode toggle persisted via `localStorage` - IntersectionObserver for fade-in animations and animated counter trigger - `requestAnimationFrame` ease-out cubic counter animation - Publication search (live text filter) + type filter buttons using `data-type` attributes - Scroll progress bar driven by `window.scrollY` - `history.replaceState` to clean URL hash without page reload - Semantic Scholar public API (`api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/author/search`) as live citation source (Google Scholar has no public API) - Fonts: Playfair Display (headings) + Source Sans 3 (body) + JetBrains Mono (metrics) - Git: separate repos, both hosted on GitHub Pages --- 3. Files and Code Sections: **`/scratch/gdemil24/samson-moges.github.io/index.html`** (829 lines) - Complete rewrite of existing file - Sections: scroll-progress bar, navbar (with theme toggle), hero (aurora BG + avatar + tags + CTA buttons), about (animated metrics grid), news (6 milestone cards), research (3 project cards + 4 interest cards), cv timeline (4 nodes), publications (search+filter+15 cards with `data-type`), contact (5 cards), footer - Nav brand changed from `href="#hero"` to `href="/"` (URL fix) - Each publication card has `data-type="journal|conference|preprint|thesis"` for JS filtering - Avatar: `` **`/scratch/gdemil24/samson-moges.github.io/css/style.css`** (1497 lines) - Complete rewrite; resolved pre-existing merge conflict - Dual theme via `:root,[data-theme="dark"]` and `[data-theme="light"]` CSS variable blocks - Key classes: `.hero-aurora`, `.aurora-1/2/3`, `.about-metrics`, `.timeline`, `.pub-controls`, `.filter-btn`, `.publication-card`, `#scroll-progress` - Responsive breakpoints: 900px (tablet), 640px (mobile), 400px (small) **`/scratch/gdemil24/samson-moges.github.io/js/main.js`** (199+ lines) - Theme toggle + localStorage persistence - Scroll progress bar - Navbar scroll shadow - Mobile nav toggle - Active nav link tracking - Animated counters (IntersectionObserver + rAF ease-out cubic) - Fade-in observer - Publication search (`input` event) + type filter (`click` on `.filter-btn`) - Footer year - **URL fix (added last):** ```javascript var navBrand = document.querySelector('.nav-brand'); if (navBrand) { navBrand.addEventListener('click', function (e) { e.preventDefault(); window.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: 'smooth' }); history.replaceState(null, '', '/'); }); } ``` --- **`/scratch/gdemil24/aleka-ayalew.github.io/index.html`** (~829 lines) - Built from scratch (repo had only an empty 1-line file) - Same structure as Samson's but personalised for Aleka: - Title: "Aleka Melese Ayalew – AI & Medical Imaging Researcher" - Nav brand sub: "AI & Medical Imaging" - Position: "Doctoral Researcher · AI & Medical Imaging" - Affiliation: CMVS, University of Oulu, Finland - Hero tags: Deep Learning, Medical Image Analysis, Computer Vision, NLP, Healthcare AI - Hero buttons: Google Scholar (primary), ORCID (outline), Academic CV (ghost), University Profile (ghost) - Metrics: 528 citations, 24 publications, 60 articles reviewed, 6 years experience - Profile photo: `` - 3 research projects: Medical Image Diagnostics, Smart IoT Healthcare, LLMs & NLP - CV timeline: 3 nodes (Doctoral 2022–present, Lecturer 2016–2022, MSc pre-2016) - 7 confirmed publications (2025×3, 2024×3, Earlier×1) with real DOI/ResearchGate links - Contact: 6 cards (email with mailto link, Scholar, ORCID, University, LinkedIn, GitHub) - Publications subtitle: "24+ publications · 528+ citations" - Nav brand changed to `href="/"` (URL fix) **`/scratch/gdemil24/aleka-ayalew.github.io/css/style.css`** - Copied verbatim from Samson's site (identical design system) **`/scratch/gdemil24/aleka-ayalew.github.io/js/main.js`** - Based on Samson's main.js with two additions: **(1) Live Semantic Scholar citation fetch (added at top, before theme toggle):** ```javascript (function fetchLiveCitations() { var url = 'https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/author/search' + '?query=Aleka+Melese+Ayalew&fields=name,citationCount,paperCount,hIndex&limit=5'; fetch(url) .then(function (r) { return r.json(); }) .then(function (data) { if (!data.data || !data.data.length) return; var best = null; data.data.forEach(function (author) { var name = (author.name || '').toLowerCase(); if (name.indexOf('aleka') === -1) return; if (!best || (author.citationCount || 0) > (best.citationCount || 0)) { best = author; } }); if (!best || !best.citationCount) return; var citEl = document.querySelector('.metric-number[data-count]'); if (citEl) { citEl.setAttribute('data-count', best.citationCount); var subtitleEl = document.querySelector('#publications .section-subtitle'); if (subtitleEl) { subtitleEl.innerHTML = subtitleEl.innerHTML.replace( /\d+\+?\s*citations/i, best.citationCount + '+ citations' ); } } }) .catch(function () { /* keep static fallback */ }); })(); ``` **(2) URL hash fix (same as Samson's, added at bottom):** ```javascript var navBrand = document.querySelector('.nav-brand'); if (navBrand) { navBrand.addEventListener('click', function (e) { e.preventDefault(); window.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: 'smooth' }); history.replaceState(null, '', '/'); }); } ``` **`/scratch/gdemil24/aleka-ayalew.github.io/aleka.jpg`** - Real profile photo committed to repo root - Replaces the inline `
` monogram placeholder --- 4. Getnet Demil AI & Remote Sensing

Doctoral Researcher · AI & Remote Sensing for Hydrology

Getnet Demil
Jenberia

CMVS / ITEE, University of Oulu, Oulu, Finland

Deep Learning Remote Sensing Snow Hydrology Computer Vision Earth Observation GeoAI
Google Scholar GitHub LinkedIn University Profile

About Me

Doctoral researcher bridging artificial intelligence and Earth observation for climate-critical hydrology challenges.

20 Citations
5 Publications
4 Years Research
6 Projects

I am a doctoral researcher at the Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering (ITEE), University of Oulu, specialising in artificial intelligence and remote sensing for hydrology modelling. My work focuses on developing deep learning methods that extract snow and water characteristics from multi-modal satellite imagery — combining Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical, and DEM data to build climate-resilient runoff prediction models.

My academic journey spans multiple continents: a BSc and MSc in electrical engineering and communication systems from Bahir Dar University, Ethiopia, followed by an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degree (IPCV) across the University of Bordeaux (France), Autonomous University of Madrid (Spain), and Pázmány Péter Catholic University (Hungary). I am currently co-organising the HydroImaging Workshop at IEEE ICIP 2026 in Tampere, Finland — a testament to my commitment to the growing GeoAI community.

Beyond academia, I have worked as a Junior Electrical Engineer at the Ethiopian Electric Utility and Chief Technology Support at the American Space Ethiopia (U.S. Embassy), grounding my research in real-world engineering challenges and cross-cultural collaboration.

Earth Observation & GeoAI

AI-driven snow & water estimation from Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical satellite data for climate-resilient hydrology.

Erasmus Mundus Scholar

EU-funded EMJMD scholarship in Image Processing & Computer Vision, studying at three top European universities across France, Spain, and Hungary.

IEEE ICIP 2026 Organiser

Co-organising the HydroImaging Workshop on mining imaging data for hydrological and environmental modelling at IEEE ICIP, Tampere, Finland.

International Experience

Studied and worked across Ethiopia, France, Spain, Hungary, and Finland — bringing a truly global perspective to AI research and engineering practice.

Latest News

Recent conference presentations, publications, and research milestones.

Nov 2025
Presentation

CrossFuse Research Presented at Digital Waters Flagship

Presented CrossFuse — a hybrid CNN-Transformer architecture for Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical data fusion for snow cover estimation — at the Digital Waters Flagship Biannual Meeting, Aalto University, Espoo, Finland.

Aug 2025
Conference

Presented research on a machine learning approach for emergency communication ecosystems at the Digital Emergency Communication (DIGeMERGE) 2025 Conference, focusing on AI-enhanced citizen participation in Nordic countries.

Jun 2025
Conference

Participated in the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR 2025), Nashville, TN, USA — the flagship venue for computer vision and deep learning research.

Publication

Journal Paper Accepted in Earth Science Informatics

2025
Publication

Systematic Review Published in Journal of Hydrology

"Advances in image-based estimation of snow variables" published in Journal of Hydrology (Elsevier). A comprehensive review of deep learning architectures for snow hydrology modelling. DOI: 10.1016/j.jhydrol.2025.132855

Oct 2024
Workshop

HydroImaging Workshop Accepted at IEEE ICIP 2026

Co-organised the HydroImaging workshop — "Mining Imaging Data for Hydrological and Environmental Modelling" — accepted at IEEE ICIP 2026, Tampere, Finland (September 13–17, 2026).

Research

Applying AI and multi-modal satellite data to advance our understanding of the cryosphere and water cycle.

Multi-Modal Satellite Data Fusion

Developing CrossFuse — a hybrid CNN-Transformer architecture that fuses Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical imagery to produce high-resolution snow cover and water equivalent estimates, supporting runoff prediction and flood risk assessment.

Sentinel-1 SAR Sentinel-2 CNN-Transformer Snow Hydrology

Deep Learning for Snow Segmentation

Designing mDeepLabV3+ — a modified DeepLabV3+ with ResNet backbone that separates snow from clouds in satellite imagery with state-of-the-art accuracy, enabling reliable year-round snow monitoring critical for water resource management.

DeepLabV3+ ResNet Semantic Segmentation Cloud Detection

AI for Climate & Emergency Response

Leveraging NLP and social media analytics for real-time local climate impact monitoring, and building AI-enhanced early warning systems that improve emergency communication ecosystems in Nordic countries.

NLP Social Media Analytics Early Warning Systems Climate AI

Research Interests

GeoAI & Earth Observation

Foundation models and vision transformers applied to large-scale satellite imagery for environmental monitoring.

Multi-Modal Data Fusion

Combining SAR, optical, DEM, and reanalysis data streams for richer environmental scene understanding.

Foundation Models for EO

Adapting large pre-trained vision models to geoscience tasks such as change detection and hydrological parameter retrieval.

Climate-Focused AI

Building data-driven tools that support climate adaptation — snow water equivalent estimation, flood mapping, and vegetation monitoring.

Projects

Selected research and engineering projects — from satellite image analysis to assistive robotics and climate AI.

CrossFuse Active

Hybrid CNN-Transformer architecture for fusing Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical satellite data to estimate high-resolution snow cover extent and snow water equivalent. The model integrates spectral band optimisation, attention mechanisms, and transfer learning to achieve superior performance on high-latitude, snow-dominated landscapes.

PyTorch Google Earth Engine Sentinel-1 SAR Sentinel-2 Transformers Python
GitHub
mDeepLabV3+ Published

Modified DeepLabV3+ architecture with ResNet-50/101 backbone for snow-cloud segmentation in Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery. Introduces dilated convolutions, optimised spectral band selection, and domain-adapted training to reliably separate snow cover from cloud cover — a persistent challenge in remote sensing.

TensorFlow OpenCV ResNet DeepLabV3+ Sentinel-2 Python
Paper (ESI)
Climate Social Media Monitor Published

Real-time NLP pipeline that mines social media streams to detect and monitor local climate impact events. Integrates transformer-based text classifiers with geo-tagged post analysis to identify floods, droughts, and extreme weather episodes as they unfold — bridging citizen science and AI for climate resilience.

NLP Transformers Social Media APIs Python SIGIR 2024
Paper (arXiv)
HydroImaging Workshop @ ICIP 2026 Upcoming

Co-organising the first HydroImaging Workshop — "Mining Imaging Data for Hydrological and Environmental Modelling" — at IEEE ICIP 2026, Tampere, Finland (Sep 13–17, 2026). The workshop brings together Earth observation, computer vision, and environmental modelling researchers. Featuring keynotes, oral sessions, and poster presentations.

IEEE ICIP 2026 Tampere, Finland Sep 2026 Workshop Organisation
Workshop Website
Smart Microscope for Disease Diagnosis Best Africa Project

Computer vision system for automated protozoan disease detection using a custom-built microscopy platform. Achieved real-time classification of blood-borne pathogens, reducing diagnostic time in resource-limited clinical settings. Recognised as the Best Project at Bahir Dar University (2018) and one of the Best 50 African Projects of the Year at Africa Innovation Week (2019).

Python OpenCV Computer Vision Medical AI Raspberry Pi
Africa Innovation Week 2019

European consortium research project developing 6D pose estimation for individuals with upper-limb disabilities. Implemented DenseFusion model (joint point cloud + RGB processing) for accurate object pose recognition in unstructured environments, enabling robotic arms to grasp everyday objects reliably for users who cannot perform the task themselves.

Deep Learning Remote Sensing Snow Hydrology Computer Vision Earth Observation GeoAI
Google Scholar GitHub ResearchGate LinkedIn University Profile

About Me

Doctoral researcher bridging artificial intelligence and Earth observation for climate-critical hydrology challenges.

20 Citations
5 Publications
4 Years Research
6 Projects

I am a doctoral researcher at the Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering (ITEE), University of Oulu, specialising in artificial intelligence and remote sensing for hydrology modelling. My work focuses on developing deep learning methods that extract snow and water characteristics from multi-modal satellite imagery — combining Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical, and DEM data to build climate-resilient runoff prediction models.

My academic journey spans multiple continents: a BSc and MSc in electrical engineering and communication systems from Bahir Dar University, Ethiopia, followed by an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degree (IPCV) across the University of Bordeaux (France), Autonomous University of Madrid (Spain), and Pázmány Péter Catholic University (Hungary). Research visits to RISE Sweden (Gothenburg) and University of Florida TREC have broadened my expertise to Nordic snow monitoring and multi-sensor tropical remote sensing.

I am co-organising the HydroImaging Workshop at IEEE ICIP 2026 in Tampere, Finland, and actively contribute to the growing GeoAI research community through publications, conference presentations, and open-source tools.

Earth Observation & GeoAI

AI-driven snow & water estimation from Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical satellite data for climate-resilient hydrology modelling.

Erasmus Mundus Scholar

EU-funded EMJMD scholarship in Image Processing & Computer Vision, studying at three top European universities across France, Spain, and Hungary.

IEEE ICIP 2026 Organiser

Co-organising the HydroImaging Workshop — mining imaging data for hydrological & environmental modelling — at IEEE ICIP, Tampere, Finland.

International Experience

Studied and conducted research across Ethiopia, France, Spain, Hungary, Finland, Sweden, and the United States — bringing a truly global perspective.

Latest News

Conference presentations, publications, and research milestones — plus blog posts from Medium.

  1. Nov 2025
    Presentation

    CrossFuse Research at Digital Waters Flagship Meeting

    Presented CrossFuse — a hybrid CNN-Transformer architecture for fusing Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical data for high-resolution snow cover estimation — at the Digital Waters Flagship Biannual Meeting, Aalto University, Espoo, Finland. Paper coming soon.

  2. Aug 2025
    Conference

    Paper Presented at DIGeMERGE 2025

    Presented a machine learning approach for AI-enhanced emergency communication ecosystems and citizen participation in Nordic countries at the Digital Emergency Communication (DIGeMERGE) 2025 Conference.

  3. Jun 2025
    Conference

    Attended CVPR 2025 in Nashville, Tennessee

    Participated in the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR 2025), Nashville, TN, USA — the flagship venue for computer vision and deep learning research worldwide.

  4. 2025 In Press
    Publication

    Paper Accepted in Earth Science Informatics (Springer)

    "Seeing through the clouds: enhanced snow and cloud segmentation in Sentinel-2 imagery with mDeepLabV3+" accepted for publication in Earth Science Informatics. DOI: 10.1007/s12145-025-01950-6

  5. 2025
    Publication

    Systematic Review Published in Journal of Hydrology

    "Advances in image-based estimation of snow variables: A systematic literature review on recent studies" published in Journal of Hydrology (Elsevier). DOI: 10.1016/j.jhydrol.2025.132855

  6. Oct 2024
    Workshop

    HydroImaging Workshop Accepted at IEEE ICIP 2026

    Co-organised the HydroImaging workshop — "Mining Imaging Data for Hydrological and Environmental Modelling" — accepted at IEEE ICIP 2026, Tampere, Finland (Sep 13–17, 2026). Keynote by Prof. Kevin Tansey (University of Leicester).

Loading posts from Medium…

Research

Applying AI and multi-modal satellite data to advance understanding of the cryosphere and water cycle.

Multi-Modal Satellite Data Fusion

Developing CrossFuse — a hybrid CNN-Transformer architecture that fuses Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical imagery to produce high-resolution snow cover and water equivalent estimates for runoff prediction.

Sentinel-1 SAR Sentinel-2 CNN-Transformer Snow Hydrology

Deep Learning for Snow Segmentation

Designing mDeepLabV3+ with dilated convolutions and ResNet backbone to reliably separate snow from clouds in Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery — enabling year-round snow monitoring for water resource management.

DeepLabV3+ ResNet Semantic Segmentation Cloud Detection

AI for Climate & Emergency Response

Leveraging NLP and social media analytics for real-time local climate impact monitoring, and building AI-enhanced early warning systems improving emergency communication ecosystems in Nordic countries.

NLP Social Media Analytics Early Warning Systems Climate AI

Research Interests

GeoAI & Earth Observation

Foundation models and vision transformers for large-scale satellite imagery and environmental monitoring.

Multi-Modal Data Fusion

Combining SAR, optical, DEM, and reanalysis data streams for richer environmental scene understanding.

Foundation Models for EO

Adapting large pre-trained vision models to geoscience tasks — change detection, hydrological parameter retrieval.

Climate-Focused AI

Data-driven tools for climate adaptation — snow water equivalent, flood mapping, vegetation monitoring.

Projects

Selected research and engineering projects — from satellite image analysis to assistive robotics and climate AI.

CrossFuse Active

Hybrid CNN-Transformer architecture fusing Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical imagery for high-resolution snow cover and snow water equivalent estimation. Integrates spectral band optimisation, cross-modal attention, and transfer learning for high-latitude, snow-dominated landscapes.

PyTorch Google Earth Engine Sentinel-1 Sentinel-2 Transformers Python
GitHub
mDeepLabV3+ Published

Modified DeepLabV3+ with ResNet-50/101 backbone for snow-cloud segmentation in Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery. Introduces dilated convolutions and domain-adapted training to reliably separate snow from cloud cover — a persistent challenge in remote sensing.

TensorFlow OpenCV ResNet DeepLabV3+ Sentinel-2 Python
Paper (ESI)
Climate Social Media Monitor Published

Real-time NLP pipeline mining social media streams to detect and monitor local climate impact events. Integrates transformer-based text classifiers with geo-tagged post analysis to identify floods, droughts, and extreme weather episodes as they unfold.

NLP Transformers Social Media APIs Python SIGIR 2024
ACM DL
HydroImaging Workshop @ ICIP 2026 Upcoming

Co-organising the HydroImaging Workshop — "Mining Imaging Data for Hydrological and Environmental Modelling" — at IEEE ICIP 2026, Tampere, Finland (Sep 13–17, 2026). Featuring keynote by Prof. Kevin Tansey (Univ. Leicester), oral and poster sessions, and panel discussions.

Computer vision system for automated protozoan disease detection using a custom-built microscopy platform. Achieves real-time classification of blood-borne pathogens, reducing diagnostic time in resource-limited clinical settings. Awarded Best Project, Bahir Dar University 2018 and Best 50 African Projects, Africa Innovation Week 2019.

EU consortium research project developing 6D pose estimation for individuals with upper-limb disabilities. - I am a doctoral researcher at the Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering (ITEE), University of Oulu, specialising in artificial intelligence and remote sensing for hydrology modelling. My work focuses on developing deep learning methods that extract snow and water characteristics from multi-modal satellite imagery — combining Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical, and DEM data to build climate-resilient runoff prediction models.

- My academic journey spans multiple continents: a BSc and MSc in electrical engineering and communication systems from Bahir Dar University, Ethiopia, followed by an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degree (IPCV) across the University of Bordeaux (France), Autonomous University of Madrid (Spain), and Pázmány Péter Catholic University (Hungary). I am currently co-organising the HydroImaging Workshop at IEEE ICIP 2026 in Tampere, Finland — a testament to my commitment to the growing GeoAI community.

- Beyond academia, I have worked as a Junior Electrical Engineer at the Ethiopian Electric Utility and Chief Technology Support at the American Space Ethiopia (U.S. Embassy), grounding my research in real-world engineering challenges and cross-cultural collaboration.

Hybrid CNN-Transformer architecture for fusing Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical satellite data to estimate high-resolution snow cover extent and snow water equivalent. The model integrates spectral band optimisation, attention mechanisms, and transfer learning to achieve superior performance on high-latitude, snow-dominated landscapes.

Hybrid CNN-Transformer architecture fusing Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical imagery for high-resolution snow cover and snow water equivalent estimation. Integrates spectral band optimisation, cross-modal attention, and transfer learning for high-latitude, snow-dominated landscapes.

Modified DeepLabV3+ architecture with ResNet-50/101 backbone for snow-cloud segmentation in Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery. Introduces dilated convolutions, optimised spectral band selection, and domain-adapted training to reliably separate snow cover from cloud cover — a persistent challenge in remote sensing.

About Me

Doctoral researcher bridging artificial intelligence and Earth observation for climate-critical hydrology challenges.

I am a doctoral researcher at the Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering (ITEE), University of Oulu, specialising in artificial intelligence and remote sensing for hydrology modelling. My work focuses on developing deep learning methods that extract snow and water characteristics from multi-modal satellite imagery — combining Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical, and DEM data to build climate-resilient runoff prediction models.

My academic journey spans multiple continents: a BSc and MSc in electrical engineering and communication systems from Bahir Dar University, Ethiopia, followed by an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degree (IPCV) across the University of Bordeaux (France), Autonomous University of Madrid (Spain), and Pázmány Péter Catholic University (Hungary). I am currently co-organising the HydroImaging Workshop at IEEE ICIP 2026 in Tampere, Finland — a testament to my commitment to the growing GeoAI community.

Beyond academia, I have worked as a Junior Electrical Engineer at the Ethiopian Electric Utility and Chief Technology Support at the American Space Ethiopia (U.S. Embassy), grounding my research in real-world engineering challenges and cross-cultural collaboration.
